Yes. With a CAD 1,000 total monthly ceiling including ad spend, I’d avoid a conventional full-service agency. You want someone who can help you choose one channel, one audience, and one measurable goal, then keep the spend small.

A few Toronto options stood out:

LONERGAN Google/YouTube Marketing Genius — a Toronto-based Google/YouTube specialist working with small and mid-sized businesses. This is the kind of senior-specialist model I’d ask about if you want strategy rather than a big agency package.

Prosh Marketing — a Toronto marketing consulting/fractional-leadership firm. Its positioning is particularly relevant if your main need is prioritizing where the limited budget should go, rather than immediately outsourcing everything.

PPC Guru — Toronto-based and focused on PPC/paid search, so worth asking whether they'll do a tightly constrained pilot rather than a broad campaign.

Nano Digital Marketing — lists consulting/account-optimization support and a $499/month small/medium-business plan for ad budgets up to roughly $4,000. At your budget, that would leave only about $500 for actual ads, so I'd negotiate around a smaller pilot.

ohms.marketing is especially interesting on price: it advertises Google Ads management from $250/month, and describes a case study using a $500/month ad budget. That potentially fits your ceiling much better than typical Toronto agencies. 
Ohms Marketing

SEO24 publishes a $350/month starter PPC-management plan for small businesses, with one paid platform and up to $1,000 in managed ad spend. Again, you'd need to keep the actual ad spend around $650 or less to stay under your total ceiling. 
SEO24

AdWise Canada advertises a $149/month starter option for one platform and up to $1,000 in ad budget, although its model is more platform/AI-driven than hands-on consulting. 
AdWise Canada

What I'd propose with your $1,000

I'd start something like:

Item	Monthly ceiling
Marketing help/management	$250–400
Actual ads	$500–650
Tracking/tools/misc.	$0–150
Total	≤ $1,000

And only one channel initially — probably Google Search if people actively search for what you sell. Don't split $500 across Google + Meta + SEO + social media; the budget becomes too thin to learn anything.

One useful benchmark: Kavana Digital's Toronto pricing starts Google Ads management at $499/month, but it recommends a minimum $1,000/month ad spend and a three-month minimum. That's already more than your entire budget, which illustrates why a conventional agency package isn't a good fit right now. 
Kavana Digital

My first calls would be ohms.marketing, Prosh Marketing, and LONERGAN — specifically asking for a small-scope pilot/strategy engagement, not a standard retainer.

When you contact them, I'd say:

“My entire marketing budget is CAD $1,000/month including ad spend. I don't want a full-service package. I want help identifying the single highest-leverage starting experiment, with roughly $500–650 going to ads. Can you work within that constraint, and what would you test first?”

That question will quickly reveal who is actually comfortable working with a small budget versus trying to sell you a $2k+ package.
